title: `st.selectbox` with many options (~16k) freezes on open in 1.59.0 — forced reflow in StreamlitMarkdown (regression from 1.58.0)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

An `st.selectbox` populated with a large number of options (~16,000) becomes effectively unusable in **1.59.0**: clicking to open the dropdown freezes the main thread for ~25 seconds. During the freeze the widget is greyed out (stale/running state) and neither clicking nor scrolling works. The same code on **1.58.0** opens the dropdown in ~0.5 s and is fully responsive.

A Chrome DevTools performance trace of the open interaction shows the time is dominated by a **forced reflow / layout thrashing**, with the top contributing call frame inside **`StreamlitMarkdown`** (plus `useFloatingOverlay` from the dropdown). On 1.58.0 the "Forced reflow" insight does not appear at all for the same interaction.

This looks like a rendering regression in how selectbox options are rendered in 1.59.0 (each option appears to go through the Markdown renderer). The 1.59 changelog includes a "fix selectbox format_func object-identity" change (#15618) which touches this code path.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# ~16k options, with a trivial format_func (mirrors a real destination-search selectbox)
options = [f"{40000 + i} - LOCATION NAME {i}" for i in range(16000)]

choice = st.selectbox(
    "Search destination",
    options=options,
    index=None,
    format_func=lambda o: o,
)
st.write(choice)
```

### Steps To Reproduce


1. Run the app above with **streamlit==1.59.0**.
2. Click the selectbox to open the dropdown.
3. Observe the widget greys out and the tab freezes for ~25 s (no click / no scroll).
4. Downgrade to **streamlit==1.58.0**, rerun, repeat: the dropdown opens in ~0.5 s and is responsive.

### Expected Behavior


Opening a selectbox with a large option list should stay responsive (as it does in 1.58.0 — ~0.5 s to open), without freezing the main thread.

### Current Behavior

On 1.59.0 the open interaction blocks the main thread ~25 s. Measured with Chrome DevTools (Performance):

- 1.58.0: interaction (INP) ~495 ms, no "Forced reflow" insight, widget stays interactive (white).
- 1.59.0: ~26 s of blocked main thread, "Forced reflow" insight ~4.4 s, top frame inside `StreamlitMarkdown` (+ `useFloatingOverlay`); widget greyed out / not clickable.

Reproduced with the minimal snippet above **in isolation** (no other app code): on 1.59.0 the selectbox never becomes interactive on open (stays greyed ~25 s); on 1.58.0 it opens immediately.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (vs 1.58.0 OK)
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:


### Additional Information

The forced reflow is dominated by `StreamlitMarkdown` — each of the ~16k options appears to be rendered through the Markdown renderer, and combined with the dropdown's `useFloatingOverlay` (which reads layout geometry) this triggers heavy synchronous layout on open. Suspected related change: #15618 ("fix selectbox format_func object-identity"), which modified the selectbox option render path in 1.59.

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15863)

This is a **frontend performance regression** in `st.selectbox` introduced in **1.59.0**: opening a dropdown backed by a very large option list (~16k) freezes the main thread for many seconds.

**Likely root cause (not the PR the reporter suspected).** The regression is almost certainly [#15438 — *Remove `BaseWeb` for `selectbox`*](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15438), which shipped in 1.59.0 (confirmed: present in `1.59.0`, absent in `1.58.0`). The old BaseWeb dropdown rendered options through `VirtualDropdown` using `react-window`'s `FixedSizeList`, so only the handful of visible rows were mounted. The new `react-aria-components` `ComboBox` implementation (`frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Dropdown/Selectbox.tsx`) renders **every** option at once via `displayOptions.map(...)` into `StyledListBoxItem`s — i.e. ~16k DOM nodes are created synchronously on open. Combined with the new `useFloatingOverlay` hook (floating-ui `flip`/`shift`/`size` + `autoUpdate`, added in [#15638](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15638)) that reads layout geometry to position the popover, this produces the "Forced reflow" / layout-thrashing the DevTools trace shows.

The reporter's suspected PR [#15618](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15618) / [#15639](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15639) ("format_func object-identity") is likely a **red herring** — that change is Python-side selection resolution and doesn't touch option rendering. The `StreamlitMarkdown` frame in the trace is most likely the widget label (or imprecise profiler attribution); the dominant cost is the un-virtualized option list. A fix should restore list virtualization for the selectbox (and likely multiselect) dropdown.

### Related Issues

- [#7104 — Allow developer to limit the max number of results to show in the `st.selectbox` dropdown to improve widget performance](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7104): Directly describes the same underlying problem — rendering thousands of DOM elements for large option lists slows the browser. Most closely related.
- [#12260 — Regression: Selectbox/Multiselect keyboard focus not activating on mobile](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12260): Another confirmed regression in the same `st.selectbox`/`st.multiselect` widgets, indicating the dropdown rewrite has introduced regressions in this area.
- [#12090 — Slow Rendering Of Large Pages (Many Widgets)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12090): Broader frontend rendering-performance issue caused by high DOM element counts; same class of bottleneck.

This will be fixed in the patch 1.59.1 that will be released today.
